content:
The quotation states Brahman "contains all works and desires and all perfumes and all tastes" and "enfolds the whole universe," indicating omnipresence and immanence in all things.  
Option (B) is incorrect because the text does not describe a paradise but rather Brahman's presence in the heart and universe.  
Option (C) is too narrow—Brahman is not only in the hearts of the faithful but "enfolds the whole universe."  
Option (D) contradicts the tone, as the text describes Brahman as loving, not vengeful.  
Thus, (A) best reflects the description of Brahman as universal and all-containing.  

Final answer: (A)
